Thanks — trying to get this to procurement by EOW.

Maya / Chris —

Appreciate you flagging this. Based on Naomi's reconciliation (attached), here's a commercial proposal to close this quickly and keep you focused on product work:

Summary numbers (prelim):
- Measured retroactive overage (June surge): 18,640 GPU-hours equivalent (reported as token-inference units in export)
- Gross one-time charge: $276,600
- Proposed goodwill credit: $41,500 (15% of overage)
- Net bill if invoiced one-time: $235,100

Top-up alternative (our recommendation):
- Convert $200,000 of the net bill into committed capacity credit applied to your next 12‑month term (effective immediately on renewal).
- Remaining $35,100 to be invoiced as a one-off settlement with standard 30-day terms.
- We will also waive the implementation surcharge and provide a 30‑day priority onboarding to shift the bursty workloads into dedicated pools to reduce recurrence.

If you accept the top-up alternative we will:
1) Draft a short amendment that adds $200k of pre-paid committed capacity to your renewal (applies as a top-up bucket, non-refundable, usable over the next 12 months).
2) Issue a revised invoice for $35,100 and apply the $41,500 credit already agreed by finance.
3) Schedule a handoff call with our infra team to optimize the endpoints and avoid retraining-triggered spikes.

Please let us know which option you prefer. If top-up is acceptable, Naomi will circulate the amendment for DocuSign and we can close by end of next week.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the math.
